title: T2T-Hub: a central platform for analyzing plant and animal telomere-to-telomere genomes.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Parsed the supplementary workbook (Table S1 = 270 complete-genome rows + 1,354 fragmented-genome rows with gap and fragment counts; Table S2 = 270 rows of contig-filtering statistics) and five live platform endpoints: the genome list (270 genomes: 231 plant, 39 animal), the file list (1,809 files, 217.5 GB total), the release metadata (270 records), the portal summary, and one full genome record (Arabidopsis thaliana Col-CEN) containing 94 assembly/metadata fields plus a 27,251-row gene table whose columns are gene_ID, source_ID, chromosome, start, end, strand, function, go, kegg, tf_family, tf_type. I also ran a threshold test on Table S1: 'gaps<=50 and fragments<=50' alone classifies complete vs fragmented assemblies at 92% accuracy.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: How each annotation column is produced (InterProScan 5.59 for domains/GO, KofamScan for KEGG, iTAK 1.8 for plant transcription factors, AnimalTFDB 4.0 HMM searches for animals, EDTA for repeats, BUSCO 5.8.0 for completeness, Biopython for protein properties), the telomere rule (>=20 copies of CCCTAAA/CCCTAA at chromosome ends) and the centromere rule (longest tandem-repeat-enriched region after trimming 100 kb ends). I could not retrieve any sequence file: the bulk download endpoint returned HTTP 500 on two payload shapes and five candidate static paths returned the single-page-app HTML instead of a file, so file sizes are from the platform's own file list, not from downloads.

a1_downloadable.note: No login or application needed and the metadata/annotation endpoints all returned real JSON; but the bulk sequence download (POST /t2thubAPI/download) returned HTTP 500 every way I tried, so the 217.5 GB of FASTA/GFF3 files is listed, not obtainable today.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Verified in the files: tf_family, tf_type, go, kegg and function are literal columns of the 27,251-row gene table; assembly summary fields (telomere counts, repeat percentages, BUSCO) are literal fields of the genome record.

a3_inputs_present.note: The model input would be sequence, and no sequence is in any table I could retrieve: protein/CDS/genome FASTA exist only as files behind the broken download endpoint, so inputs would have to be re-fetched from each genome's original source link (270 separate external archives).

a4_units_stated.note: Coordinates in base pairs, repeat content as explicit percentages, lengths in Mb; minor gaps, e.g. the genome list's 'length' (599.56) and 'rate' (79.31%) fields carry no unit label.

a5_enough_rows.note: Gene level is large (27,251 genes in the one genome I pulled, 270 genomes available); but the comparative genome-level table is only 270 rows, far under the threshold for any cross-species regression.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~1 GB of gene tables (270 API records) or ~16 MB per genome for one GFF3 + protein FASTA
a6_fits_laptop.note: The full listed collection is 217.5 GB (110 GB of it InterProScan output), but single-genome subsets are small; no GPU needed for a tabular baseline.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Close but not exact: paper says 230 plant + 39 animal, the live genome list returns 231 plant + 39 animal = 270, the supplement lists exactly 270 complete genomes, and InterProScan output exists for 269 of 270.

a8_label_provenance.note: Fatal and verified: every candidate label is another program's output computed from the same sequence that would be the input - transcription-factor family from iTAK/AnimalTFDB HMM rules, GO from InterProScan, KEGG from KofamScan, repeat fractions from EDTA, centromere position from tandem-repeat scanning, telomere counts from a motif scan, protein properties from Biopython. No physical measurement exists anywhere in the resource.

existing_models.name: T2T-Hub's own pipeline (this paper): rule-based telomere motif scan plus longest-tandem-repeat centromere call
existing_models.score_and_split: No accuracy reported; the authors state centromere calls are 'indicative' and need experimental validation. Its assembly filter (gaps <= min(2n,50)) is justified on the 270 vs 1,354 genome supplement, where I measured a two-column threshold reaching 92% accuracy.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Centromere prediction for centromeres that lack tandem-repeat structure, and extending advanced analyses to user-uploaded genomes.

existing_models.name: CentIER, a machine-learning centromere identifier for plant genomes (2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported by its authors as roughly 24% better accuracy and 28% better F1 than quarTeT on Arabidopsis, rice, maize, soybean and mulberry; found via search, abstract-level only.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved beyond the abstract summary.

existing_models.name: quarTeT, a telomere-to-telomere toolkit with a centromere predictor (Horticulture Research 2023)
existing_models.score_and_split: Used as the comparison baseline by CentIER; no held-out-species benchmark retrieved.

existing_models.name: MegaPlantTF, a machine-learning framework for plant transcription-factor identification and family classification (2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: k-mer protein representations plus a deep network and stacking ensemble; scores not retrieved beyond the abstract. It targets exactly the tf_family column this resource would supply.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Coverage and scalability of existing domain-rule tools such as iTAK.

existing_models.name: iTAK (2016), the domain-rule transcription-factor classifier whose output IS the tf_family column here
existing_models.score_and_split: Rule-based (required/forbidden Pfam domains), no learned weights, no held-out benchmark.

backbone.name: Nucleotide Transformer / DNABERT-2 (DNA) or ESM-2 (protein)
backbone.hardware: CPU for ESM-2 small checkpoints on a per-genome protein subset
backbone.licence: Backbones permissive; the T2T-Hub paper itself is CC BY-NC (non-commercial).

integration.partner_dataset: UniProt / Pfam-InterPro (via source gene IDs such as AT1G01010) and NCBI Taxonomy (taxonomy IDs are present, e.g. 3702)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Could ask whether repeat and centromere architecture across 270 complete genomes predicts gene-family expansion, but with 270 genomes and tool-derived variables on both sides the combination cannot be tested honestly.

controls.positive_control: Predicting protein length or molecular weight from sequence would pass trivially, but here it is not a control - molecular weight is itself one of the resource's computed columns.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is runnable on the gene tables.
controls.external_validation: PlantTFDB and AnimalTFDB would serve as a second source for transcription-factor families, but both are built from the same domain-rule logic as the labels here, so agreement would prove nothing.

honest_claim_h3: Any model trained on this resource would claim only 'I can reproduce what InterProScan, iTAK and a tandem-repeat scanner output when run on this sequence', because no label in the resource is a measurement.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a gene's protein sequence to predict its transcription-factor family and functional annotation across 270 complete genomes.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-gene rows from the platform's gene tables (27,251 genes verified for one genome, 270 genomes listed), each with a family label and functional terms; the sequence itself would have to be fetched separately because the download endpoint is broken.
plain_idea.predict: The transcription-factor family and Gene Ontology/KEGG terms. The 'true answer' is not a measurement: it is whatever iTAK, AnimalTFDB hidden-Markov-model searches, InterProScan and KofamScan printed when run on the same sequence.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It would not be: the model's ceiling is the annotation tool's accuracy and it would never reveal where that tool is wrong. The useful thing learned here is that a uniformly annotated genome collection is not the same as a labelled dataset.

more_or_better_data.why: 270 genomes with tool-derived annotations is not more or better than what iTAK, InterProScan or MegaPlantTF already train/run on; the annotations here were produced BY those tools, so the data is downstream of the competition, not ahead of it.

confidence_score.why: No replicate measurements exist anywhere - each genome is annotated once by one pipeline, so there is no noise estimate to calibrate against.

models_beatable.why: You cannot beat iTAK or InterProScan on labels they generated; agreement with them is the ceiling, by construction. CentIER (2024) and MegaPlantTF (2025) are recent and already address the centromere and transcription-factor tasks.

guaranteed_improvement.why: The baseline tool defines the labels, so our model can at best tie it; the condition 'the label measures the same quantity independently of the baseline' fails outright.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict transcription-factor family / Gene Ontology terms from sequence across 270 telomere-to-telomere genomes, or predict centromere position from DNA. Both labels are the output of the pipeline that produced them (iTAK, InterProScan, tandem-repeat scanning) run on the exact input sequence, so the project would distil a hidden-Markov-model search rather than learn biology. The one genuinely tabular supplement (270 complete vs 1,354 fragmented assemblies) is solved at 92% accuracy by a two-column threshold I ran myself, and its label is definitionally the same thing as its features.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: scraping 270 genome records at roughly 3 MB of JSON each (the Arabidopsis record alone was a 27,251-row gene table) gives about 1 GB; sequences were unobtainable so no embedding cost could be estimated.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Ask of each column 'what instrument measured this?' - the paper's own Methods answer every time is a software tool run on the same sequence (InterProScan, KofamScan, iTAK, EDTA, BUSCO, Biopython, a motif scan). Five minutes in the Methods kills it.

verdict_reason: Fails A8: every label in the resource is a bioinformatics tool's output computed from the sequence that would be the model's input (transcription-factor family from iTAK, Gene Ontology from InterProScan, centromeres from tandem-repeat scanning), so any model would distil those tools rather than learn biology. A3 also fails - no sequence is retrievable because the bulk download endpoint returns HTTP 500 - and the only comparative table is 270 genomes, far too few, while the 1,624-row supplement is solved by a two-column threshold at 92% accuracy.
